explanation: Shrunk scenario is single fast body (vx~45 m/s) approaching a thin horizontal wall (h=0.28 < diameter 1.0, top y=5.526) at grazing y ~5.5. With dt=0.00306 and 5 substeps, semi-implicit Euler displaces ~0.138m/step (~0.027m/substep). Body is outside at step 16 (distance +0.097), lightly penetrating at step 17 (distance -0.040 within tolerance) and accumulates penetration to -0.178 at step 18 exceeding 0.15 limit without effective impulse/positional correction. Thin wall + high tangential speed causes discrete penetration to grow before collision response activates, likely because collision is treated as point contact on thin edge and substep/correction is insufficient for grazing fast contacts.
vision_note: The red circle moves horizontally at the height of the thin dark wall and makes contact with its left tip around step 16-17. By step 18 it is visibly embedded/overlapping the tip of the wall instead of bouncing or sliding cleanly along it, remaining intersecting the wall edge.
